subject: Intermittent route blackholing after on-prem peering switchover
messages:
From: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Team,

We completed the staged peering switchover this morning (03:00 UTC) and starting at ~03:05 UTC several of our services reported "connection timed out" to the onprem app cluster (10.10.0.0/22). The alerts show packets reaching your edge but then flows intermittently drop with no ICMP TTL-expired or TCP RSTs.

Quick facts:
- Affected subset: app-cluster-3 (10.10.2.0/24)
- Origin: Keystone datacenter -> transit -> Redwood peering
- Time window: 03:05 - ongoing, intermittent (spikes every ~5-10 minutes)
- We ran a couple traceroutes that show hops stop at your edge (attached).

Can you confirm whether anything in your switchover automation could have left stale next-hops or NAT rules? Also seeing a few MTU fragmentation hints in captured packets.

Attaching: keystone_traceroute_20270503.txt (traceroute output)

Thanks,
Kevin
PeerOps - Keystone Energy
(attachment: keystone_traceroute_20270503.txt)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Kevin — thanks for the heads up and the trace. I'm triaging now. Quick requests so we can narrow this down:

1) Paste the full traceroute output (including TTL counts) and one example of a failing TCP handshake (client -> 10.10.2.12:443), or a pcap if you have it.
2) Do you see any BGP flaps on your side around 03:00 UTC?
3) Which onprem gateway IP are you steering to (we want to validate next-hop reachability)?

Marissa / Mateo — can you pull kernel counters and BGP adj states for the edge that handled Keystone's peer (edge-id: edge-us-west-12)? Please check:
- ip route show for 10.10.0.0/22
- show bgp neighbors
- conntrack table size and nat table hits
- dmesg for any frag/MTU noisy logs

I'm putting this on the urgent list and will escalate to networking infra if we see route instability.

-Lauren
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Reference runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networking/private-peering-triage

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Checked edge-us-west-12 now. Initial findings:

- BGP: adj(s) stable, no flaps recorded around 03:00 UTC (show bgp neighbors: Established for >12h).
- Route table: 10.10.0.0/22 is present and points at next-hop 198.51.100.22 (to Keystone gateway).
- Kernel: conntrack high watermark increased at 03:06 UTC for ephemeral NAT entries, but we are not hitting max_conntrack.
- NAT: iptables MASQUERADE rule exists for 10.10.0.0/22 on postrouting chains.
- dmesg: repeated "IPv4: packet too large" messages around 03:05 — likely MTU/MSS related.

I applied a temporary static route on the edge to prefer next-hop 198.51.100.22 via vlan-2 (was learned via bgp but we force-installed to remove any potential RIB/ECMP oscillation).
Status immediately improved for ~7 minutes in our internal checks.

Attaching the traceroute you sent and a quick snippet of the edge routing table (attachment: keystone_traceroute_20270503.txt).

Next steps proposal:
- Ask Keystone to capture a client-side pcap of a failing handshake.
- Schedule a short maintenance window to: 1) patch MTU on GRE/encap path (increase to 9000 or set MSS clamp), 2) tighten BGP next-hop validation and disable an ECMP path that is intermittently dropping large frames, 3) validate NAT port allocation patterns for high ephemeral churn.

Will hold off on permanent changes until we have the pcap and confirm schedule.

-Marissa
Senior NetOps, Redwood Inference
(attachment: keystone_traceroute_20270503.txt)

From: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Marissa — thanks, attaching one pcap and a sample failing client TCP handshake. The traceroute lines show the last responding hop is your edge, then stars thereafter. We also see TCP MSS ~1420 on SYN which would be consistent with an encapsulation overhead (GRE/VXLAN).

Excerpt from traceroute: 
 1 192.0.2.1 0.9 ms
 2 198.51.100.22 1.4 ms
 3 * * *

PCAP: keystone_segment_capture_01.pcap (contains client->10.10.2.12 SYN and no SYN-ACK returned).

We did the switchover to a new onprem gateway (198.51.100.22) as part of cutover automation. We can roll back but would prefer a fix on your side if possible.

-Kevin
(attachment: keystone_segment_capture_01.pcap)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

All — good data, thanks. Given that a forced static made traffic pass for a short window and collated dmesg shows "packet too large", two parallel root causes look likely: a) ECMP/RIB oscillation where some dataplane path is dropping encapsulated frames, and b) MTU/MSS mismatch on the encapsulation path.

Immediate actions I'm authorizing now:
- Marissa, hold the static route you installed for now (we need it until we can deploy a stable change).
- Mateo, can you push an MSS clamp on the forward path at edge-us-west-12 to 1400 and enable per-flow path pinning for the affected prefix to avoid ECMP churn? Use our hotfix playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networking/mss-clamp-hotfix
- Marissa, after Mateo's change, monitor health for 30 minutes; if stable, coordinate a maintenance window with Keystone for a permanent MTU increase + BGP next-hop sanity checks (proposed May 10 02:00 UTC).

Also we should document this as a known cutover checklist item for future onprem peer flips (add MTU/MSS and port-churn validation). I'll open NET-4821 and link the artifacts.

-Lauren

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: NetInfra Pager <netinfra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: Edge us-west-12 MSS clamp & per-flow pinning (urgent)

NetInfra team, please triage immediately — see thread and attachments. Pager: NET-4821 is the ticket.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Kevin — we applied the MSS clamp + per-flow pinning at 10:58 PDT and are watching. Early telemetry: SYN success rate to 10.10.2.12 improved from ~62% -> 98% over the next 8 minutes. No more "packet too large" messages in dmesg.

Proposed permanent plan (May 10 02:00 UTC maintenance):
- Update GRE/VXLAN MTU to 9000 end-to-end where possible, or set consistent MSS clamp profile for endpoints that cannot support jumbo frames.
- Run a BGP next-hop validation pass and remove any stale ECMP path that has >5% drop.
- Add an entry to the peer cutover checklist to capture pcap/traceroute pre/post cutover and run a quick MTU/MSS sanity test.

I'll update NET-4821 with the captures and command outputs. Thanks for the quick coordination — let us know if you want us to rollback the cutover while we schedule the maintenance.

-Marissa
Senior NetOps, Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Barnes <peerops@keystone-energy.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peering switchover - intermittent connectivity to onprem app cluster

Appreciate the rapid response—holding cutover state for now. May 10 maintenance window works for us; please share the exact UTC window once scheduled and we'll coordinate our change board.

-Kevin
